solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An innocent lawyer's letter

blocks.note: a lamb is a byword for an innocent person
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A naive solicitor sends a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An innocent' looks like an adjective for the lawyer, but it is a noun of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A short hearing for courts

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A brief legal hearing held in the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' looks legal, but it means courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court in a building, and the plural is atria.

clue.text: A single addition to the CV?

definitions.text: A single addition to the CV?

blocks.clueFragment: A single addition to the CV?
blocks.note: surface reading: just one extra line on a résumé
setter's reading: a single person is unmarried, giving the possessive of an unmarried man, and the addition is a qualification

explanation.walkthrough: 'single' seems to mean one, but it means unmarried, and an unmarried man's qualification is a first university award.
explanation.definitionFit: A first university qualification, such as a BA, is listed on a CV, and its name includes the word for an unmarried man.

clue.text: A drowned youth's buried by Pope

indicators.note: what is buried lies inside, so the youth's name holds the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach Hero
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'by', as in three by four

explanation.surface: A boy who drowned is laid to rest beside the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like 'next to', but it is the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander was the name taken by several popes, and also the first name of the poet Pope.

clue.text: Pirate shot, beheaded, put ashore

indicators.note: losing the head means the opening letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: a shot is a photograph, informally a pic
to maroon someone is to abandon them on a shore

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is shot, decapitated and dumped on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' sits next to 'shot' but applies to the following word, which loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaroon is an old word for a rogue or sea robber, a synonym of pirate.

clue.text: Hefty bill for this road feature?

blocks.clueFragment: Hefty bill for this road feature?
blocks.note: surface reading: an expensive invoice for building some roadworks
setter's reading: a bird with a huge beak, whose name labels a kind of pedestrian crossing

explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' suggests money, but it is a bird's beak; the bird with the biggest beak names a British signal-controlled crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain this is a road crossing where pedestrians press a button to change the traffic lights.

clue.text: Sound of insect that's caught fly, almost

indicators.note: almost all of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
to fly is to rush or hurry

explanation.surface: The buzz of an insect that has just snapped up a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect's prey, but it is a verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A churr is a low trilling call, made by crickets, nightjars and other creatures.

clue.text: A street magician's mad rush to finish

indicators.note: something mad is wild and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: all fifteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A busker conjuror hurrying frantically to finish the act.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a desperate effort to complete something before a deadline.

clue.text: It's hard to return from this public hearing

blocks.clueFragment: It's hard to return from this
blocks.note: surface reading: a place one struggles to come back from

blocks.clueFragment: It's hard to return from this
blocks.note: setter's reading: in tennis, a shot into the unguarded part of the court is very difficult to hit back

explanation.walkthrough: 'return' suggests coming back, but in tennis it is hitting the ball back; a shot placed into the space a player has left is hard to reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing held where the public and press may attend is said to take place in this setting.

clue.text: Toss the nuclear bombs from this

definitions.text: Toss the nuclear bombs from this

indicators.note: to bomb is to blow apart, so the following words are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: to toss, as a ship does on waves, is to rock
these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to fire nuclear bombs from a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description: bombs are tossed from such a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket launcher is a weapon that fires explosive missiles, which the whole clue depicts.

clue.text: How a gentleman's acquired a salary

indicators.note: the phrase has acquired, or holds within it, the letters wanted

blocks.note: the end of 'How', 'a' and the start of 'gentleman' run together

explanation.surface: A question about how a gentleman came by his income.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is regular pay for work, close in sense to a salary.

clue.text: Minute is not quite seven days

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its final letter

blocks.note: seven days make a week

explanation.surface: A minute falls short of a full week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like a unit of time to match the days, but it is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is a Scottish word for small, so it matches minute in the sense of tiny.

clue.text: Keeping ball with Bill and Gordon Bennett up front

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
both are British exclamations of surprise
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Keeping a ball in play alongside a man called Bill and one called Gordon Bennett.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' places the bill and the exclamation before the ball. 'Gordon Bennett!' is British slang for an exclamation like 'blimey', as is 'cor'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In accordance with' means in keeping with, so the noun matches 'keeping' in that sense of agreement.

clue.text: Throw me around in front of study's fire

indicators.note: turning around means the preceding words are read back to front

blocks.note: to lob is to throw
taken as written
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be hurled about by the hearth in a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like a noun for the study's hearth, but it is a verb meaning to inspire.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to inspire courage in them, the same as making them bolder.

clue.text: Gargle what, so hum is removed?

indicators.note: something removed is moved out of place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about gargling to get rid of a bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' reads as taken away, but split as re-moved it means moved again.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargle is a liquid rinsed around the throat, so it is a synonym for an oral rinse.

clue.text: Disease, extremely painful, and fever

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters
ague is a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A description of an illness that is very painful and feverish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plague is an epidemic infectious illness, such as bubonic plague.

clue.text: Letters and numbers of letters

blocks.note: surface reading: alphabet characters and how many of them there are
setter's reading: codes made of letters and digits that route mail

explanation.walkthrough: The second 'letters' means mail, not characters.
explanation.definitionFit: A British address code such as SW1A 1AA mixes characters and digits to direct mail.

clue.text: Item on display I swear can be heard

indicators.note: what can be heard is judged by sound, not by spelling

blocks.note: one who swears is a curser, so 'I swear' describes one

explanation.surface: Someone vows that an exhibited object is audible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I swear' sounds like an oath, but it is the speaker identifying as someone who curses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursor is the pointer or blinking marker shown on a computer screen.

clue.text: Sound of hooter about to be carried by judge

indicators.note: turned about means the word is flipped end to end
what is carried is held inside the bearer

blocks.note: hooter is British slang for a nose
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: The noise of an owl or a car horn about to be brought before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of hooter' suggests a homophone, but 'Sound' alone is the definition and 'hooter' is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To resonate is to sound out with a deep, echoing ring.

clue.text: Queen and king informally training RAF member

blocks.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Royals casually drilling a member of the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two royal pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Erk is British slang for an aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank, or a raw recruit.

clue.text: Notes on staff not bound to be used

definitions.text: Notes on staff not bound to be used

blocks.clueFragment: Notes on staff not bound to be used
blocks.note: surface reading: memos for employees that need not be acted on
setter's reading: musical notes on a stave, printed on loose unbound pages

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees and 'not bound to be used' suggests optional, but a staff is also the five lines of music, and loose pages are not bound into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Music printed on single loose pages for performers is known by this name, as opposed to a bound score.

clue.text: Circling earth, atmosphere was lower

indicators.note: to circle something is to go round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a mood is an atmosphere or feeling
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: As it orbited our planet, the air pressure dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' looks like the comparative of low, but it is one who lows, like a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make a cow's noise, so a lower is a cow and 'was lower' is past tense of that sound.

clue.text: Heading off to hunt rabbit

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to stalk prey is to hunt it

explanation.surface: Setting out to hunt a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like the quarry, but it is British slang: to rabbit on is to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage to rabbit means to chatter at length, so it is a slang synonym.

clue.text: See rising smoke — reason?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a cig is a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: Is there a reason for the smoke climbing upwards?
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, so it is a synonym for reason as a noun.

clue.text: Unremarkable song Tom Petty covers

indicators.note: something that covers others wraps around them

blocks.note: fiddling means trivial or petty
an air is a tune or song
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dismissive review of a forgettable track that Tom Petty covered.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Petty looks like the singer's name, but the surname is the outer word, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only moderately good, neither great nor bad, is described by this phrase, a synonym for mediocre.

clue.text: One drives over fields with those following track

blocks.note: people who follow blindly are sheep
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: A motorist crossing fields, followed by a convoy along a track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drives' suggests a car, but here it means herding livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A working collie herds flocks across pasture, so driving animals over fields is what it does.

clue.text: Outline of small boat

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: The silhouette of a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or summary, so it is a synonym of an outline.
